title: Temporal variation and chemico-biological profiling of bioactive metabolites from  Pinus wallichiana : experimental and computational mechanistic insights
content: The present study investigates the phytochemical analysis, seasonal variation, and therapeutic potential of essential oils EO(s) extracted from Pinus wallichiana needles during summer, autumn, and winter seasons, complemented by experimental and computational insights. The study investigates experimental analyses with computational approaches. Gas chromatography-Mass Spectrometry (GC-MS) and 13C NMR spectroscopy identified 27, 25, and 20 constituents in the summer, autumn, and winter EOs respectively. The oil yields ranged from 0.21% to 0.35% across the seasons. The major components were α-pinene (25.56–36.6%), β-pinene (29.96–31.17%), and d-limonene (3.91–9.24%). The EOs exhibited potent anti-tuberculosis and anti-helminthic activities, with IC50 values of 0.1 mg mL−1 and 20 mg mL−1, respectively, comparable to standard drugs. To further validate their therapeutic potential, molecular docking, 100 ns MD simulations, and molecular mechanics/generalized Born surface area (MM/GBSA) analyses were performed for several metabolites against four key therapeutic targets of Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) and Haemonchus contortus: DprE1, dihydrodipicolinate synthase, PMT1, and Tubulin-TUB015. d-limonene emerged as the most promising lead metabolite, exhibiting the strongest binding affinities for DprE1 (−9.3 kcal mol−1) and Tubulin-TUB015 (−8.2 kcal mol−1). Subsequent MD and MM/GBSA results confirmed the high stability and favourable binding energetics of the complexes. Overall, this integrated approach supports the therapeutic potential of P. wallichiana EOs and provides a robust molecular basis for their further development as natural antitubercular and anti-parasitic agents.
